AWARD 1.

Vide this order I shall dispose off the present claim filed by the petitioners under Section 166 &
140 of Motor Vehicles Act (hereafter referred to as 'M.V. Act'), however, during the dependence, on an application moved by the petitioners, which was allowed vide order dated 02.03.2020 and the present petition was converted into petition under Section 163A of M.V. Act.
DAR was also filed in the present matter, which was merged with the present petition vide order dated 07.04.2018.

2. Brief facts of the case are that on 23.12.2017, Dilshad (hereafter referred to as 'victim') was going on foot and at about 9.30 am when he reached at flyover Mukarba Chowk, Jahangir Puri, meanwhile a bus No. DL1PD 2992, driven by its driver at a very high speed, rashly and negligently came and hit the victim. As a result of which victim fell down on road and sustained injuries.
Victim was taken to BJRM Hospital.
However, victim could not survive and succumbed to the injuries.

sentences.text: 4. Respondents no.1 and 2 had contested the claim by filing their joint written statements stating that accident had occurred due to negligence on the part of victim.

It is further stated that their bus was duly insured with respondent no. 3 and hence liability to pay compensation to the petitioners, if any, is of respondent no. 3.
5.
Respondent no. 3 in its written statement has not disputed the vehicle of respondent no. 2 was insured with it on the date of accident.
However, it has taken the similar plea that accident had occurred due to negligence of victim himself.
It further denied its liability on technical grounds as well.

6. It is pertinent to mention here that during the pendency, respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co.
had given an offer of Rs. 3 lacs on 25.09.2018 which was accepted to the petitioner by making a statement, however later on, the petitioners did not come forward to receive the said amount and were not ready to settle the matter for the offered amount and matter was taken up for further proceedings as per the law.

Whether the deceased Sh. Dilshad suffered fatal injuries in road traffic accident on 23.12.2017 at about 9.30 a.m. at Flyover Bus Stand, Mukarba Chowk, Jahangirpuri, Delhi due to involvement of bus bearing No. DL-1PD 2992 being driven by respondent no. 1 Bal Kishan, owned by Sh. Shiv Kumar and insured with respondent no. 3 Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.?

OPP.

9. I have heard Ld. counsel for petitioners & respondents and perused the record carefully and thoroughly.

My issuewise findings are as under: ISSUE No.1: Whether the deceased Sh. Dilshad suffered fatal injuries in road traffic accident on 23.12.2017 at about 9.30 a.m. at Flyover Bus Stand,
Mukarba Chowk, Jahangirpuri, Delhi due to involvement of bus bearing No. DL1PD 2992 being driven by respondent no. 1 Bal Kishan, owned by Sh. Shiv Kumar and insured with respondent no. 3 Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.? OPP.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.
PW1 Rani Kha / petitioner no.1 has deposed in terms of the claim petition that on 23.12.2017, her brother (victim) met with accident with bus No. DL1PD 2992 and died.

As the present petition was converted under Section 163A of Motor Vehicles Act, and as per Section 163A (2) of M.V. Act, rash and negligent driving is need not to be proved and the relevant section is reproduced for a ready reference.

Section 163A (2) of M.V. Act In any claim for compensation under sub-section (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or permanent disablement in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or vehicles concerned or of any other person ...

Accordingly,
this issue is decided in favour of the petitioners by holding that victim died due to vehicular accident occurred on 23.12.2017 at about 9.30 a.m. at Flyover Bus Stand, Mukarba Chowk, Jahangirpuri,
Delhi due to involvement of bus bearing No. DL1PD 2992.

ISSUE No.2: Whether the LR's of deceased are entitled to any compensation if so to what amount and from whom.
11.
Petitioner no. 1/PW1 has proved that the deceased was 20 years old at the time of accident and was doing private job and earning Rs. 40,000/ per annum.

She further stated that she being sister,
Riayajudden & Irshaid being brothers are the only legal heirs of deceased as the deceased was unmarried and their parents are predeceased to their brother Dilshad (victim).

As there is no cloud on the fact that the petitioners are not the legal representatives of the deceased as nothing contrary has been brought on record by the respondents or the investigating officials, therefore, they are entitled to file the petition.

sentences.text: Now, coming to the aspect of entitlement of compensation by the petitioners.

Admittedly the petitioners are sister and brothers of deceased and being sister and brother, who are major in age on the day of accident, so, they are not entitled to the compensation on account of loss of their dependency upon the deceased.

In terms of Sarla Verma Vs. DTC 2009 ACJ 1298 SC, as such there is no dependent upon the Rani Kha & Ors, Vs. Bal Kishan & Ors.
deceased and the petitioners therefore would be entitled to the compensation for loss of estate only.
In Keith Rowe Vs. Prashant Sagar & Ors MAC. APP. No. 601 / 2007 decided on 15 January-2010

sentences.text:
the Hon'ble High Court has summarized the law with respect to such cases where LRs is/are not financially dependent upon the deceased as under:
"
(i) The law contemplates two categories of damages on the death of a person.
The first is the pecuniary loss sustained by the dependent members of his family as a result of such death.
The second is the loss caused to the estate of the deceased as a result of such death.

In the second category, the action is brought by the legal representatives, on behalf of the estate of the deceased and the compensation,
when recovered, forms part of the assets of the estate.
(ii) Where the claim is by the dependents, the basis for award of compensation is the loss of dependency, that is loss of what was contributed by the deceased to such claimants.

A conventional amount is awarded towards loss of expectation of life,
under the head of loss to estate.

(iii) Where the claim by the legal representatives of the deceased who were not dependents of the deceased, then the basis for award of compensation is the loss to the estate, that is the loss of savings by the deceased.
A conventional sum for loss of expectation of life, is added.
(iv) The procedure for determination of loss to estate is broadly the same as the procedure for determination of the loss of dependency.
Both involve ascertaining the multiplicand and capitalising it by multiplying it by an appropriate multiplier.

But,
the significant difference is in the figure arrived at as multiplicand in cases where the claimants who are dependents claim loss of dependency, and in cases where the claimants who are not dependents, claim loss to estate.

The annual contribution to the family constitutes the multiplicand in the case of loss of dependency, whereas the annual savings of the deceased becomes the multiplicand in the case of loss to estate.
The method of selection of multiplier is however the same in both cases."

Though the quantum of savings will vary from person to person, there is a need to standardize the quantum of savings for determining the loss to estate (where the claimants are not dependents) in the absence of specific evidence to the contrary.

The quantum of savings can be taken as one-third of the income of the deceased where the spouses are having a common establishment and one- fourth where the spouses Rani Kha And Ors vs Bal Kishan And Ors on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194193889/
6 are having independent establishments.

entities.text: Rani Kha And Ors vs Bal Kishan And Ors on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon

sentences.text: The above will apply where the family consists of non-dependent spouse/children/parents.
Where the claimants are non-dependent brothers/sisters claiming on behalf of the estate, the savings can be taken as 15% of the income.
The above percentages, one of course, subject to any specific evidence to the contrary led by the claimants."
13. Now coming to the multiplier aspect.
There are three petitioners in this matter and as it has already been discussed herein above that petitioners are entitled to compensation on account of loss of estate only.
In view of the findings in Keith Rani Kha & Ors, Vs. Bal Kishan & Ors.

Rowe (Supra) it has also been settled that multiplier would however remain same and it is only the head under which the petitioners would likely to succeed would change.
Now, the second part of the issue in hand with respect to the quantum of compensation is to be adjudicated and below are the finding: -
14.
In claim petitions filed under Section 163A of Motor Vehicles Act, annual income of deceased can only be taken to be 40,000/ per annum and not more than that.
There is no future prospects given in the claim petitions filed under Section 163A, hence income as Rs. 40,000/ per annum is taken for calculating the future loss of earning.
As per the Adhar Card of victim his birth year is 1997, which means that victim was 20 years of age at the time of accident.

So, a multiplier of 18 is taken for calculating loss of dependency as per judgment in Sarla Verma (supra).
15.

Counting in this way, the total loss of dependency comes to Rs. 1,08,000/ (7,20,000 - 85% =
1,08,000/).
Accordingly, this amount of Rs.1,08,000/ is allowed to the petitioners, as loss of dependency.

16. Apart from amount mentioned above, petitioners are granted a sum of Rs.2,000/ for funeral expenses and Rs.2,000/ for loss of estate and petitioner no.1 is separately granted a sum of Rs.5,000/ for loss of consortium, making a total sum of Rs.1,17,000/ detail of which is given in the attached proforma.

In the light of the above discussion, the aspect of liability of the respondents is to be adjudicated and findings are mentioned below: -
17.

sentences.text: Hence, respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has failed to establish any statutory defence on record.
Further, it is matter of record that during the pendency, respondent no. 3 / Ins. co. has given offer of Rs. 3 lacs and even statement of both the Ld. counsels was recorded to that effect.
However, later on, petition was converted into Section 163A of M.V. Act.
All this shows that respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has no statutory defence and is liable to indemnify the insured and to pay the above said compensation to the petitioners.
This issue is, therefore, decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents by holding that respondent no.3 / Ins. Co. is liable to pay the amount of compensation to the petitioners.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Rani Kha And Ors vs Bal Kishan And Ors on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194193889/
3 3.
Contending that said accident occurred and victim died due to involvement of aforesaid vehicle,
the petitioners have filed the present claim petition thereby claiming a compensation of Rs.
50,00,000/ from Bal Kishan (hereafter referred to as 'respondent no. 1'), Shiv Kumar ( hereafter referred to as 'respondent no. 2'}, driver & owner of the vehicle involved in the accident and from the Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. (hereafter referred to as 'respondent no. 3').
Rather, Rani Kha & Ors, Vs. Bal Kishan & Ors.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
As the present petition was converted under Section 163A of Motor Vehicles Act, and as per Section 163A (2) of M.V. Act, rash and negligent driving is need not to be proved and the relevant section is reproduced for a ready reference.
Rani Kha & Ors, Vs. Bal Kishan & Ors.
10.
In these circumstances, without going into the aspect of rash and negligency of the driver of the vehicle by which the accident was caused and taking note of the mandatory provision of the above mentioned section, it is established that there is no dispute regarding the death of the deceased and of the involvement of the vehicle which was driven by the driver at the time of accident.
As there is no cloud on the fact that the petitioners are not the legal representatives of the deceased as nothing contrary has been brought on record by the respondents or the investigating officials, therefore, they are entitled to file the petition.
Rani Kha And Ors vs Bal Kishan And Ors on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194193889/
5 12.
Admittedly the petitioners are sister and brothers of deceased and being sister and brother, who are major in age on the day of accident, so, they are not entitled to the compensation on account of loss of their dependency upon the deceased.
In terms of Sarla Verma Vs. DTC 2009 ACJ 1298 SC, as such there is no dependent upon the Rani Kha & Ors, Vs. Bal Kishan & Ors.
deceased and the petitioners therefore would be entitled to the compensation for loss of estate only.
In Keith Rowe Vs. Prashant Sagar & Ors MAC. APP. No. 601 / 2007 decided on 15 January-2010
There are three petitioners in this matter and as it has already been discussed herein above that petitioners are entitled to compensation on account of loss of estate only.
In view of the findings in Keith Rani Kha & Ors, Vs. Bal Kishan & Ors.
In claim petitions filed under Section 163A of Motor Vehicles Act, annual income of deceased can only be taken to be 40,000/ per annum and not more than that.
There is no future prospects given in the claim petitions filed under Section 163A, hence income as Rs. 40,000/ per annum is taken for calculating the future loss of earning.
The petitioners Rani Kha & Ors, Vs. Bal Kishan &
Ors.
have made the respondent no.3 (insurance company) as party, seeking direction that respondent no.3 / Ins. Co. be directed to pay the compensation to them.
Hence, respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has failed to establish any statutory defence on record.
However, later on, petition was converted into Section 163A of M.V. Act.
All this shows that respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has no statutory defence and is liable to indemnify the insured and to pay the above said compensation to the petitioners.
